A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original synthetic-data experiments, including approximation-error curves and attention heatmaps in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: Section 5 retains these original synthetic-data experiments and their results in Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds a three-attention-layer construction comprising token-wise pre-activations, attention-based mixing across tokens, and signed-ReLU aggregation, with padding and positional channels. This is an additional architectural construction; the original single-head, multi-head and two-layer constructions remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic truncated-linear-model and global sequence-to-sequence tasks. The additional in-context-learning discussion and Appendix G provide theory, not new evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: The experimental comparisons retain the same attention configurations and introduce no new baseline. The ReLU network remains a target-data generator rather than an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The experiments retain their sample counts, 80/20 splits, input distributions, MSE evaluation, model dimensions and training budgets. The settings accompanying Figures 2–4 are unchanged apart from cross-references.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same interpolation-count, interval-width and head-count sweeps, plus the same attention-heatmap analysis. No additional empirical ablation, robustness test or case study appears in the appendices.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and 4 retain means and one-standard-deviation bands over 10 random-seed runs. Figure 3 retains seed 1234 and three displayed test samples. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 reuse identical empirical plot content, including curves, uncertainty bands and heatmaps. The accompanying approximation-error trends and qualitative observations are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds a lemma for implementing sequence-wise linear maps with attention and a three-layer universality theorem with proofs. v2 also adds explicit precision/temperature bounds and complexity derivations. Theorem 3.1 drops v1's exceptional-region qualification, although its appendix restatement retains that restriction for general output-index mappings.

C1.justification: The central two-layer universality, single-layer-plus-softmax and in-context gradient-descent claims remain. The introduction and conclusion additionally advertise an extension closer to standard Transformer architecture, developed in Appendix G. Moving the existing gradient-descent theorem into Section 4 does not constitute a new contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the account of practical applicability: it distinguishes nonstandard sequence-wise maps from token-wise Transformer operations and discusses exponential head and parameter requirements in Remarks C.1–C.2. Appendix B.2 adds task-composition and multistep-learning interpretations. The limitation concerning in-context universality remains.

D1.justification: Remark E.3 and Corollary E.1.1 provide explicit anchor-count and temperature choices for target accuracy; Appendix G specifies padding, positional channels and projection matrices for its construction. Experimental implementation details remain unchanged, and both versions link to the same code repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2025), expands comparisons with in-context universality research, and corrects the description of Yun et al.'s depth dependence. Citations to Dai et al., Von Oswald et al. and He et al. disappear. The principal attention-only positioning remains.

P1.justification: The theoretical narrative is substantially reorganized: in-context gradient descent moves into a dedicated main section, truncated-linear in-context approximation moves to Appendix B, and activation examples move to Appendix F. v2 adds a roadmap and rewrites substantial explanatory material, particularly the two-case proof discussion in Appendix E.2.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with labels aligned to proof steps and a substantially expanded caption. v2 adds a notation table and shaded or boxed theoretical statements. Figures 2–4 retain their graphical content, with changes chiefly to placement and references.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation, explains architectural restrictions and makes precision choices explicit. However, Appendix G's new signed-ReLU proof asserts an incorrect softmax limit: an inactive diagonal score ties the padding score at zero, leaving a nonzero value contribution rather than the claimed zero output (printed pages 99–100). This undermines the added universality argument. The exposition gains and new theoretical reliability problem prevent a confident judgment of net improvement.
